neutral_facts.value: The accused, the husband of the deceased, was charged with causing the death of his wife, who died from burn injuries. The prosecution alleged that the deceased was subjected to physical and mental torture by her husband and in-laws for not providing sufficient dowry. The accused claimed that his wife had left behind a suicide note stating that she committed suicide due to harassment by her parents, not by her husband or in-laws. The trial court convicted the accused under Sections 304 and 498A of the IPC, citing harassment and cruelty. The High Court acquitted two other relatives but upheld the conviction of the accused. The Supreme Court reviewed the case, noting that the demand for Rs.50,000/- by the accused for a computer was not a dowry demand as it was not connected to the marriage. The court also found that the suicide note, written by the deceased, cast doubt on the prosecution's claim of harassment and cruelty. The court ultimately acquitted the accused, stating that the prosecution failed to prove the essential ingredients of the offenses beyond reasonable doubt.

quotes.text: The wife of appellant died due to burn injuries. The prosecution alleged that ever since her marriage, the deceased was subjected to physical and mental torture by her husband and in-laws and they all brutally assaulted her on innumerable occasions for not getting sufficient dowry.
The accused claimed that his wife had left behind a suicide note stating that she committed suicide due to harassment by her parents, not by her husband or in-laws.

The Trial Court, however, disbelieved the defence and convicted the appellant and his other relatives under Sections 3048 and 498A, IPC holding that the deceased was subjected to torture and harassment by the accused, mainly for the reason that an amount of Rs.50,000/-was not given to the appellant by the father of the deceased (PW1).
The High Court acquitted the two other relatives of the appellant (A2 and A3) but maintained the conviction of the appellant under Sections 3048 and 498A, IPC and therefore the present appeal.

The Court held: 1. The evidence of the father and mother of the deceased, viz. PW1 and PW4 is that the demand of Rs.50,000/- by the appellant was made six months after the marriage and that too for purchasing a computer to start his own business.
